title: [Treatment of locked chronic posterior dislocation of the shoulder].
journal: Sportverletzung Sportschaden : Organ der Gesellschaft fur Orthopadisch-Traumatologische Sportmedizin

sections.label: INTRODUCTION
sections.text: The posterior locked shoulder dislocation is a rare injury that is often associated with an impression fracture of the anteromedial aspect of the humeral head. The majority of posterior shoulder dislocations are missed on the initial examination.

sections.label: METHODS
sections.text: We demonstrate the case of an athlete, who presented with a posterior shoulder dislocation after a trauma two months ago.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: The patient was treated with a M. subscapularis transfer in the reverse-hill-sachs-lesion.

sections.label: DISCUSSION
sections.text: The diagnosis of the posterior shoulder dislocation remains a problem in the clinical setting. Treatment is based on the size defect of the anteromedial humeral head. Different treatment options are still controversially discussed.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: To diagnose a posterior shoulder dislocation correctly a standard clinical and radiological assessment is necessary.
